title: App organization is baffling
content:
Recent changes in the app design baffle me. Why is “bonus puzzles” at the very top now? “Bonus” implies “additional” or things you do AFTER the main attraction. If it comes before, it’s not a “bonus,” it’s the main attraction.

Speaking of the main attraction, that is and always has been the NYT Crossword, one of the most well-respected crosswords in the world. So why is it now halfway down the list instead of at the top like it used to be?

Also why do I get pop-ups advertising particular games in the app…while I’m already in the app? Just let me play what I want to. I understand if there’s something brand new you want to draw attention to, but that’s the only circumstance in which that makes sense. (But is not the only circumstances in which you get pop-ups…)

Just completely baffling decisions all around and it makes me feel like NYT’s games department has lost sight of what they’re doing and what makes their brand special.

author: Jack 00005
title: Sudoku
content: The sudoku interface is not intuitive or consistent.  As a player of sudoku using many apps I can tell you what makes your interface more difficult to use.  When a ‘normal’ number is entered and it is a candidate in that number’s row, column or square, it should be deleted as a candidate.  Most other apps work this way, which eliminates extra work and more chances to make errors.  If the developers played other sudoku games, they could see how your interface is lacking in this regard.  In addition, there are two ways a player is notified when an error is made: a red dot is put in the erroneous box or the error counter is incremented. If the error counter is not checked visually after every move, a player can easily make several moves before noticing a wrong one has been made, which may result in being unable to solve the puzzle.  I hope this helps to improve your version of sudoku to the level of your other games.  Thanks!

author: GalenMcQ
title: Changes that hurt longtime fans
content:
I have a 1600+ crossword streak, looking forward to 5 years. And in fact, I’ve been a NYT crossword player for many years, first on paper, then via early desktop apps, and then as an early adopter of this app. I’ve watched it evolve into a generally lovely platform with tons of quality of life fixes. It’s a very important part of my day, every day.

But the wheels started falling off the wagon awhile back when the stats display for crossword times split daily, best, and average into different pages, sacrificing readability and basic data visualization principles for a “cool” UI. That was a bummer, but I moved on.

Now, two days ago, I nearly had a panic attack opening the app to find the crossword GONE. My streak, surely in shambles, my daily routine, destroyed. But no, the crossword has just been demoted to below the fold, under other games I barely care about. The flagship NYT game for decades is now, I guess, an afterthought to…Tiles? How disappointing.

I used to pop open the app to quickly check that I’d kept up with my daily streak with a quick glance. Now I open the app to a burst of anxiety, knowing I can’t count on that quick check to keep up with almost 5 years of unbroken progress.

I can forgive overlooking the crossword when doling out cool badges to Wordle and Spelling bee. I got over the abysmal solve time charts. But this might do me in. For goodness’ sake, put the crossword back at the top where it belongs or at the VERY least let me re-order the games on my own device!

title: Crossword Completion Screen “X” Issue Workaround
content:
6/29/26 - The “X” issue in crossword puzzles has yet to be fixed. Even after several ‘updates’. 


The issue many of us are contending with is as far as I can determine has to do with the iPhone Display Zoom setting being set to “Larger Text”. 
If you go to your Settings app, then “Display & Brightness”, scroll down to “Display Zoom” and toggle it to “Default”. Then click the Blue Check. You then get a pop-up that says ‘Changing Display Zoom will Restart iPhone’, click ‘Standard’. Screen will go dark for a few seconds as display resets (it doesn’t ‘restart’ your phone btw). 
You now will be able to dismiss the crossword completion screen by clicking the X in upper right corner, as the game was designed to do. 
Only downside is you lose the ‘Larger Text’ effect on the iPhone until you toggle it back. 
I tried creating an automation that would be able to do the aforementioned falderal with a click or too but no luck. Alas ….
I truly wish the NYTimes Games dev team would fix this glitch.
